items.hook: Lattice QCD puts the nucleon light sigma term at 53.0 MeV, with a 7.4 MeV statistical error.

readout.label: Nucleon light sigma term, lattice QCD

items.summary: Simulations with four lattice spacings at physical pion mass are extrapolated to the continuum, giving the light, strange and charm sigma terms of the nucleon, which measure how quark masses contribute to nucleon mass. The strange value is 58.2 MeV and the charm value is 112 MeV. The charm term has a large uncertainty, about 28 MeV statistical.
items.title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum

items.hook: Every red-blue coloring of the plane with no red unit-distance pair contains a blue line of seven points.
items.hook_turn: contains a blue line of seven points.
items.summary: The authors improve the known unavoidable line from five points to seven, where consecutive points are one unit apart. They also prove results for three-colorings, higher dimensions and other shapes such as a regular pentagon. The proofs combine averaging inequalities, Fourier and linear-programming methods, and a measure theorem from OpenAI's Hadwiger-Nelson work. Longer lines are still unresolved.
items.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory for Lines and Finite Configurations

items.hook: A satellite-altimetry foundation model forecasts ocean eddy centers 15 days ahead to within 25.2 km.
items.summary: HaiRuo, a 1.05-billion-parameter model pretrained on 24 years of altimetry, forecasts sea level, velocity and eddy tracks from 30 days of maps. It cuts 15-day centre error 18% against fourteen other methods. Evaluation uses eddies identified from altimetry itself, so it measures agreement with that product, not independent ocean observations.
items.title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model

items.hook: Chemotaxing amoebae use 0.25% of the molecule-uptake limit, so counting noise, not energy, limits sensing.

readout.label: Dictyostelium uptake relative to sensing limit

items.summary: The authors derive formulas linking gradient-sensing accuracy to the number of absorbed molecules and the entropy that absorption produces. Re-analyzing Dictyostelium chemotaxis data places the cell far below the limit with minor metabolic load. The conclusion rests on a theoretical model and on previously published data from one organism.
items.title: Energetic costs of reaching the physical limits of sensing

items.hook: Every large enough integer is represented by Sun's ternary quadratic polynomial, with a computable bound.
items.summary: The paper proves an asymptotic version of a conjecture by Zhi-Wei Sun: all sufficiently large integers take the form x(5x+1)+y(5y+1)/2+z(5z+1)/2. The proof links the problem to a ternary quadratic form, modular forms and class number bounds, showing the genus average dominates the cusp contribution. It covers only large integers, so the full conjecture for small values still needs separate checking.
items.title: Sun's conjecture on a certain ternary quadratic form

items.hook: Weak solutions of the defocusing energy-critical Schrodinger equation are unique, with no extra assumptions.
items.summary: The paper proves that global weak solutions of the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrodinger equation are unique. It derives an energy defect threshold condition that energy conservation carries along the strong solution flow, then applies this to get unconditional uniqueness for the quintic Gross-Pitaevskii hierarchy. The result is for the defocusing case with specific nonlinearity, not general equations.
items.title: Uniqueness of global weak solutions for the defocusing energy-critical NLS

items.hook: A conjecture about balls inside shapes fails in three or more dimensions, where the radius r/2 is optimal.
items.hook_turn: where the radius r/2 is optimal.
items.summary: The strong union of uniform closed balls conjecture, recently proved in the plane, is false in every dimension n of 3 or more. The author builds compact sets from simplices whose circumcenter and incenter coincide, containing a point outside every ball of radius slightly above r/2. This shows the known radius r/2 cannot be improved in high dimensions, unlike the planar value r/sqrt(3).
items.title: A counterexample to the strong version of the union of uniform closed balls conjecture in dimensions three and higher

items.hook: UTe2's metamagnetic transition appears to end at a quantum critical point near 75 tesla.

readout.label: Field of proposed quantum critical endpoint

items.summary: Magnetization and magnetostriction of the heavy-fermion material UTe2 in pulsed fields up to 60 T point to a quantum critical endpoint at about 70 degrees from the b axis and 75 T. A pseudo-gap in the susceptibility accompanies the transition. The endpoint lies beyond the measured field range and is extrapolated, and the link to field-induced superconductivity remains speculative.
items.title: Thermodynamic signatures of a nearby quantum critical endpoint in UTe$_2$ under intense magnetic field

items.hook: Lightning's negative leaders advance as thin conducting filaments, not streamers as long assumed.
items.summary: LOFAR radio measurements of high-altitude negative leaders show the fan at the tip is made of thin filaments about 1 m in radius that grow smoothly over hundreds of meters and radiate steadily in VHF. This conflicts with the common picture of streamers at the tip. The conclusion is inferred from radio imaging of a limited set of events, not direct optical views of the filaments.
items.title: Filamentary dynamics in fan-like structures in high-altitude lightning discharges

items.hook: Graphs with n^(1+o(1)) vertices contain every n-vertex graph from any proper minor-closed class.
items.hook_turn: contain every n-vertex graph from any proper minor-closed class.
items.summary: For any fixed proper minor-closed graph class, the authors construct a graph with n^(1+o(1)) vertices and edges containing every n-vertex graph of the class as an induced subgraph. This extends earlier results for planar graphs and beats the previous O(n^2) vertex bound. It is an existence result whose bounds hide a sub-polynomial factor, and it is purely theoretical.
items.title: You Can Have It All: Small sparse induced-universal graphs for minor-closed classes

items.hook: Maximal Chebyshev hyperelliptic curves are fully classified, tied to when p generates a unit group.
items.hook_turn: tied to when p generates a unit group.
items.summary: The paper lists every prime p and finite field over which the hyperelliptic curve y^2 = phi_d(x), built from Chebyshev polynomials, is maximal. For p congruent to 1 mod 4 and odd d, maximality happens exactly when d is a power of a prime l congruent to 1 mod 4 and p generates the unit group mod d. The proof uses Shimura-Taniyama and L-series nonvanishing, and covers only primes not dividing 2d.
items.title: A Complete Classification of Maximal Hyperelliptic Curves Related to Chebyshev Polynomials

items.hook: Magnetar 1E 2259+586 spun down abruptly in 2025 as its X-ray flux doubled.

readout.label: Persistent X-ray flux increase after anti-glitch

items.summary: X-ray data from EP, NICER and IXPE show a 2025 anti-glitch in the magnetar 1E 2259+586, its largest, with a fractional frequency change near -8.19e-7. Unlike its 2019 event, the persistent flux rose by about 106% and took over 320 days to recover, with a gamma-ray burst nearby in time. The claim that fractional amplitudes grow monotonically rests on very few events.
items.title: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery

items.hook: Rational points on Cayley's cubic surface grow like B(log B)^6, matching Peyre's prediction.
items.summary: Counting rational points of bounded height on the four-nodal Cayley cubic surface, with its nine lines removed, gives N(B) asymptotic to a Peyre constant times B(log B)^6. The proof parametrizes by universal torsors and combines lattice counting with Poisson summation. The result holds for the open subset only and for the maximum-coordinate height.
items.title: Counting Rational Points on Cayley's Cubic Surface

items.hook: An LLM-assisted proof raises the proven minimum rope length for tying any knot with C crossings.
items.summary: The shortest rope that can tie a knot of unit thickness has a proven lower bound, and this paper lifts its coefficient from 1.105 to 2.0996 times C^(3/4) for crossing number C. A second bound ties length to stick number, L at least pi(s-1), which tightens bounds for at least 41 torus knots. The author worked with a chatbot and says it failed on many other problems. Only lower bounds improved; upper bounds are unchanged.
items.title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem

items.hook: On a disk, clumping cells generically blow up once mass reaches 4 pi, and never below it.
items.summary: The Keller-Segel model describes cells that attract each other through a chemical signal. The authors prove that on a disk, mass of at least 4 pi sends an open dense set of starting densities to blow-up or unbounded growth over infinite time, while lower mass always settles to a smooth equilibrium. They extend sharp thresholds to other planar domains, the sphere and the square torus. It is a mathematical result for one idealized model.
items.title: Generic singularity formation in two-dimensional Keller-Segel systems

items.hook: Fundamental groups of special quasi-projective varieties are virtually nilpotent of class at most two.
items.summary: The paper proves a conjecture of Cao, Deng, Hacon and Paun: the fundamental group of a special quasi-projective complex variety, in Campana's sense, has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index and class at most two. Known examples show two cannot be lowered. The proof builds a second Albanese map and shows its kernel on fundamental groups is finite, using minimal models. It is a highly specialized result that applies only to special varieties.
items.title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties

items.hook: A record with no entanglement can hold long-range information that only entangled measurements can read.
items.hook_turn: that only entangled measurements can read.
items.summary: Qubit probes locally record whether neighboring Ising spins on a square lattice point the same way, giving a fully separable record. Guessing the relation of two distant spins stays at chance for any separable readout when the probe overlap parameter p is at most 1 minus 1/sqrt2, yet a joint readout beats chance at distance for p of 0.29181 or more. The result is a theoretical proof for an idealized model, with no experiment.
items.title: Reading long-range information from a separable quantum record requires entangled measurements

items.hook: A DECam archive search yields 65 outer Solar System candidates, four of them possible Neptune Trojans.
items.summary: The author linked single-night detections in the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2 and confirmed candidates with forced photometry on other archival nights, leaving 65 solid candidates. Four are candidate L4 Neptune Trojans, and none beyond 80 au was confirmed, so Planet Nine is barely constrained. End-to-end recall is only about 7% and no selection function is given, so the sample cannot yield population statistics.
items.title: An Archival Search for Outer Solar System Objects in the NOIRLab Source Catalog DR2: 65 Candidates, Including Four L4 Neptune Trojans

items.hook: Heating dense matter shrinks the density range that perturbative QCD allows for neutron stars.
items.hook_turn: that perturbative QCD allows for neutron stars.

readout.label: DD2 density excluded by pQCD at entropy 5

items.summary: Earlier work showed perturbative QCD limits the equation of state of cold dense matter. The authors extend the bound to finite temperature along fixed entropy per baryon, finding the allowed region shrinks as temperature rises; for the DD2 model the limit falls from 1.0 to 0.74 per cubic femtometer. By entropy per baryon 4, seven of eleven mean-field models are excluded at six times saturation density. The bound is theoretical and depends on the extrapolation assumptions.
items.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter

items.hook: Finding the shortest vector in some structured lattices is NP-complete, shown by a reduction from Subset Sum.
items.summary: The authors prove that exact shortest-vector decision in the l-infinity norm is NP-complete for principal ideals and rank-two free modules over power-of-two cyclotomic rings, which are lattice structures used in cryptography. They give a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum and extend it to related cyclic rings. The result concerns exact solutions in one norm, so it does not break or certify any cryptosystem.
items.title: $\mathsf{SVP}_\infty$ Is NP-Hard for Power-of-two Cyclotomic Ideals

items.hook: Modulating a magnetic field makes polaritons emit photon pairs, not undergo a superradiant transition.
items.summary: Earlier predictions said modulating the magnetic field could drive a superradiant transition in Landau polaritons. An exact theory including the Faraday-induced electric field shows the system stays stable above a Krein frequency and below it emits pairs through the dynamical Casimir effect, with up to 5 to 10 dB of squeezing. The conclusion comes from theory and does not report an experiment.
items.title: Dynamical Casimir emission from Floquet-driven Landau polaritons: Gauge invariance forbids a superradiant phase transition

items.hook: Directed graphs can be sparsified to about n log n arcs, down from n log^5 n, keeping every degree.
items.summary: A singular-value sparsifier reweights a subset of a directed graph's arcs so degrees are exactly preserved while matrix behavior is approximately kept. The paper proves that O(n log n / epsilon^2) arcs always suffice, improving the earlier log^5 n bound, and gives a randomized construction running in near-linear time. This is a theoretical bound with no experiments reported.
items.title: Directed Singular-Value Sparsifiers with $O(n \log n/\epsilon^2)$ Arcs

items.hook: Lensed gravitational waves could warn of neutron-star mergers hours to days ahead, in simulation.
items.summary: Gravitational lensing can delay and repeat a merger signal so telescopes get early warning. The authors simulate lensed binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole mergers detectable in the O5 run and compute LSST light curves, finding about 60% of BNS kilonovae and 10% of NSBH kilonovae visible in one exposure. This is a population simulation built on model assumptions, not an observation.
items.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts

items.hook: SFQ pulses can steer a fluxonium qubit at over 99.99% fidelity, in simulation.
items.summary: Pulses from superconducting digital circuits, designed for transmons, work poorly on low-frequency fluxonium qubits. The authors propose two pulse protocols, one using flux-channel pulse packets and one mixing flux and charge pulses, and test them in multilevel simulations. Results are simulation only, with no hardware demonstration.
items.title: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits

items.hook: A thin film of YbSb2 shows quantum oscillations along one crystal axis and none along the other.
items.summary: Epitaxial YbSb2 films show oscillations from a Dirac-like surface state only when current runs along the a-axis. Transport, Raman and coherent phonon measurements plus first-principles calculations link this to a density-wave instability. The surface-state assignment rests on calculations, and the density-wave link is inferred rather than directly imaged.
items.title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$

items.hook: Line-photon scattering falls 4 to 9 times short of explaining the MeV feature in GRB 221009A.
items.hook_turn: falls 4 to 9 times short of explaining the MeV feature in GRB 221009A.
items.summary: The paper tests whether electrons upscattering line photons, such as H2 emission seen by JWST, could produce the MeV spectral feature in this record burst. Spectral calibration shows the best case roughly fits, but seed photon density is too low by factors of about 4 to 9 even under ideal assumptions. The models rely on assumed geometry and UV budget.
items.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A

items.hook: A 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus cannot exist, narrowing a 15-vertex record.
items.summary: A known triangulation uses 15 vertices, and it was conjectured minimal. The author rules out 13 vertices by combining a g2 inequality, a reduction to a nine-vertex model, fundamental group analysis and Alexander duality. The 14-vertex case, needed to prove minimality, stays open.
items.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus

items.hook: On-chip resistive loads reset transmon qubits in about 48 ns without exposing them to warm wiring.
items.summary: Dissipation units, resonators coupled to resistors on the chip, reset several transmons and clear leakage out of the third level. A 400 ns pulse leaves 0.29% and 0.67% residual excited population from the two starting states. Results come from a small multi-qubit device and are not yet tested inside full error-correction cycles.
items.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation

items.hook: A very general cubic threefold is stably birational only to copies of itself.
items.hook_turn: stably birational only to copies of itself.
items.summary: Voisin shows that any smooth cubic threefold stably birational to a very general one must be isomorphic to it, and the method also covers the sextic double solid and quartic threefold. This is an algebraic geometry proof. It covers very general members only, not every cubic threefold.
items.title: On the stable birational type of Fano threefolds

items.hook: Water ice grains form spontaneously around negative ions in a cold lab plasma, with no dust needed.
items.summary: In a weakly ionized plasma with trace water cooled below about 200 K, ice grains formed without dust seeds and not without ionization. Mass spectrometry showed hydrated negative ions, mainly OH- with water, growing before rapid ice growth. The result is a lab analog, and extension to the mesosphere and protoplanetary disks is an estimate.
items.title: Nucleation of water ice under weak ionization via clustering on negative ions

items.hook: Progression-free sets in any finite group are now bounded by a stronger size limit.
items.summary: The paper transfers sharp bounds on 3-term-progression-free sets from abelian groups to class 2 nilpotent groups and then to all finite groups. Combining this with a recent result by Raghavan gives a bound of |G| times exp(-c (log|G|)^(1/6) / (loglog|G|)^(1/3)). It is an upper bound only, and likely not tight.
items.title: Progression-free sets in class $2$ and arbitrary finite groups

items.hook: Lithium niobate chips modulate 493 nm light beyond 50 GHz, with 2.9 dB/cm loss.
items.summary: The team built a thin-film lithium niobate chip for blue light with couplers, splitters, rings and modulators, aimed at trapped-ion control. Modulators reach over 20 dB extinction and ring resonators show 2.9 dB/cm loss. Photorefraction and substrate uniformity remain unsolved obstacles to scaling.
items.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm

items.hook: Explicit restricted isometries now reach sparsity m^(2/3), beating the old m^(1/2) barrier.
items.summary: The authors build explicit matrices with the restricted isometry property at sparsity k near m^(2/3), using a strongly regular graph, Gershgorin's circle theorem and an incidence result of Zahl. They also show the Gram-matrix-magnitude technique's barrier is m^(2/3), not m^(1/2). Sparsity remains below the m level that random matrices reach.
items.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$

items.hook: Stars wrapped around a negative-mass core can be stable and more compact than regular polytropes.
items.summary: Solving the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations gives shells around a negative-mass singularity, called singustars. Radial mode analysis finds stable ones for Gamma = 2 up to compactness about 0.25, and nonlinear runs show collapse or dispersal depending on the perturbation. These are theoretical objects, and negative mass is not known to exist.
items.title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars

items.hook: A 63-qubit processor simulated electric flux strings in a 2D lattice gauge theory.
items.summary: Researchers evolved strings with static or dynamical charges on superconducting qubits and observed rapid spreading when deconfined and suppressed spreading at strong fields. Gauss-law constraints, ancilla checks and noise rescaling controlled errors through up to 15 Trotter steps. The model is a small Z2 theory, not the full forces of nature.
items.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor

items.hook: Riemann zeta zeros come closer than 0.7892 of the average spacing, proved without assumptions.

readout.label: Proven small-gap constant lambda_0 for zeta zeros

items.summary: Selberg showed a positive proportion of Riemann zeta zeros sit closer than the average spacing by some factor lambda_0 below 1. Using an unconditional version of Montgomery's pair correlation method, Lamzouri proves lambda_0 = 0.7892 works, versus 1 minus 2.36e-6 before. The statement says a positive proportion exists, not how large it is.
items.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function

items.hook: A fair, truthful trading mechanism always captures at least half the possible gains from trade.
items.hook_turn: at least half the possible gains from trade.
items.summary: The paper proves a mechanism with incentive compatibility and budget balance captures at least half of first-best gains in multidimensional two-sided markets. The proof uses duality and Markov chains stopped by exponential clocks. The half guarantee is tight already for one item, and it assumes additive values and independent agent types.
items.title: Second-Best Trade Is Half Efficient in Multidimensional Markets

items.hook: A planar Brownian path's sausage has about T/(r^2 (log T)^2) holes on average.
items.summary: The expected number of holes in a thickened planar Brownian path is pinned to order T/(r^2(log T)^2) for long times. The proof prices the ways near-critical pockets can form along the path's two independent arms, and also separates which holes matter at leading order. It is a pure-math estimate of order, so exact constants are not determined.
items.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage

items.hook: Zeros of the p-adic Eisenstein series E2 have j-invariants in finite unramified extensions of Q_p.
items.summary: For each prime p of at least 5, the zeros of Katz's E2 series give a handful of j-invariants, and all of them live in finite unramified extensions of the p-adic numbers. The authors use the supersingular polynomial and hypergeometric congruences, and also bound isogenies between zeros. Whether a non-CM zero can have an algebraic j-invariant stays open.
items.title: Zeros of Katz's p-adic Eisenstein series E2

items.hook: A protein-ligand language model shows binding-site skills it was never trained for.

readout.label: Dose-response hit rate, de novo compounds

items.summary: Bonbon, trained only on paired protein-ligand sequences, picks out mechanism of action, binding sites, and covalent versus non-covalent binding without task labels. These abilities jump at the largest of six model sizes, and a wet-lab test on nine targets gave a 61.5% hit rate on new compounds. It is a single-author preprint, and the wet-lab results have not been independently replicated.
items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
